# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A; text itself not needed)

## Format / source info
- Book 1: "Jimmy Quixote: A Novel" by Tom Gallon (Gutenberg #41754; publ. Hurst and Blackett, London, 1906). Dedication to Malcolm Watson. Sections: BOOK I (Ch I–VII), BOOK II (Ch I–IX), END OF BOOK I / END OF BOOK II. (A "BOOK III" heading also appears inside Book 2's file? No: Book 1 file ends "THE END" after Book III, Ch I–VI.) Structure: Book I ch I–VII; Book II ch I–IX; Book III ch I–VI.
- Book 2: "The Crow's Inn Tragedy" by Annie Haynes (Gutenberg #75307; Dodd, Mead 1927). Chapters I–XXIV, ends "The End".

## BOOK 1 — Jimmy Quixote

### Book I
**Ch I "Old Paul's Babies"**: Old Paul (Paul Nannock), tall, light brown thinning hair, back from London late July with parcels; porter at Daisley Cross. Housekeeper PATIENCE (old woman, bossy, shawl gift). ANTHONY DITCHBURN (rusty black, peevish, tobacco-dependent, "full-flavoured" tobacco mix-up). Children: MOIRA (dark-eyed, ~8, Paul's adopted daughter, mother was Paul's lost love; surname Nannock), JIMMY (boy ~12–13, cricket bat & fishing rod gift; James Larrance), ALICE (fair, blue eyes, prim; mother Mrs. Vickery, left at Daisley Place). Paul's backstory: lost love (woman with dark eyes) left him for richer man; she died, sent for him; he took baby Moira. Jimmy's parents drowned at sea; guardian embezzled, found shot in Liverpool. Alice's mother left her, never returned. Moira's shawl gift for Patience. Night visit: Moira comes to Paul's room barefoot.

**Ch II "And Old Paul's Friends"**: Ditchburn arrived stormy night, stayed (claimed to write monumental work). Quarrel over Moira. Rector REV. TEMPLE PURDUE (small, mild, widower; wife's headstone) teaches children; son CHARLIE PURDUE (wild, mischievous, ~Jimmy's age). Baffalls: DANIEL (Mr. Baffall, grey beard, "Daniel") and FLORA/MRS. BAFFALL (childless, sentimental). Honora Jackman introduced by Baffalls (loud, eyeglass, "rusticate", ~£150 a year).

**Ch III "Jimmy Quixote"**: Jimmy (13) infatuated with Honora; she kisses him, wins his help to find Paradise (secret woods glade, fir cones). Old Paul refuses; Jimmy: "You're a beast!" Paul coins name "Jimmy Quixote" after Don Quixote. Honora dinners; Paul's "Eloping" plan later. Honora leaves in Ch V.

**Ch IV "The Eloping Persons"**: Moira: "what do you do when you love anybody?"; Paul and Moira elope on the ANCIENT ONE (donkey, bought from gipsy) and old chaise (17 shillings), inn breakfast; Moira makes him promise never to elope with anyone but her. Honora sees them at the gate; Ditchburn complains about "dangerous" woman.

**Ch V "Jimmy's Affections"**: Honora's farewell dinner, sings; kisses Moira in bed while Moira pretends sleep. Station farewell to Jimmy; letter signed "Honora Jackman... yours ever lovingly." Jimmy's brief passion ends. Charlie kisses Moira in race; Jimmy fights Charlie in woods (Jimmy wins, Charlie says "I'm sorry... she isn't worth this"). Moira hides.

**Ch VI "Mrs. Baffall's Dream"**: Paul goes to London twice; learns he is dying (heart/illness, "It's death"). Night, he visits Mrs. Baffall, confides; "Good-night" not "good-bye."

**Ch VII "Over the Hills and Far Away"**: Paul dies at foot of stairs, writes unfinished will "To Moira, beloved of my heart now and always, I give—". Patience weeps; Moira reads note in study; Anthony Ditchburn tobacco-starved. Alice goes to Baffalls; Baffalls take Alice; Moira with Patience; Mr MATTHEW SHANDLER (second cousin, claims estate; thin, cadaverous, mincing) takes all; Jimmy sent to London to Baffall's business. Burial; Honora had children kept away. Moira visits grave: "Good-bye, Old Paul." Jimmy leaves over hill in rain; kiss.

### Book II
**Ch I "The Call of the World"**: Patience and Moira in Chelsea rooms (Locker Street later), Moira's life drab. Opera Faust outing with a girl; Moira writes to Alice; Alice (now "Alice Vickery") replies; Baffalls in London. Warehouse (Cheapside) - Jimmy gone. Moira sees Alice: cold, "Aunt Baffall." Clerks say Jimmy left.

**Ch II "Jimmy—and a Matter of Food"**: Jimmy in Camden Town boarding-house, shoe fight, writes; editor at a paper (flaxen-haired, pale boy WILLIAM); editing for 16s; paper folds. Holborn room; British Museum tea shop.

**Ch III "The Complete Letter-Writer"**: Patience writes letter to Alice (boastful, black-edged) claiming prosperity; Baffalls suspect bluff. Rector writes Charlie; Baffall suggests Patience take Charlie. ANTHONY DITCHBURN begs from Purdue (letter, 1 sov.). Charlie visits Moira in Chelsea ("Charlie!" x3).

**Ch IV "The Man in Print"**: Charlie takes Moira to dinner, music hall (Bohemia), cab; Ditchburn at Charlie's; Charlie moves into rooms below. Ditchburn finds Jimmy's story in print "By James Larrance"; Moira writes to Jimmy; Jimmy's reply.

**Ch V "Another Taste of Bohemia"**: Jimmy and Moira reunite in Jimmy's room; Moira pays for breakfast (eggs and bacon, frying pan); landlady; Charlie and Ditchburn arrive; Jimmy's five guineas cheque; lunch.

**Ch VI "Charlie Plunges"**: Charlie's debts; father sends £50 (last); Charlie proposes to Moira; they sleep together; Moira ashamed (pregnant). Charlie tries to borrow from Patience.

**Ch VII "Dreams"**: Jimmy's novel rejected; publisher (big-bearded) loses money; BENNETT GODSBY (actor) wants play; Moira visits Jimmy, says she'll marry Charlie; Jimmy declines.

**Ch VIII "The Sides of the 'Buses O!"**: Play written with Godsby (joint authorship, cheque £10 twice); rehearsals; Godsby's wife; Mrs. Baffall and Alice visit theatre; Alice courts Jimmy.

**Ch IX "The Dawn"**: Play opening. Moira goes to theatre, not admitted; returns; sleeps in Charlie's room; Charlie takes her; dawn, she flees.

### Book III
**Ch I "It'll Be All Right"**: Moira pregnant; Patience told; Charlie goes to father, refused ("Get out of my house"); Charlie drinks, hit by cart; dying, asks for Jimmy.

**Ch II "Jimmy Quixote"**: Jimmy's second play, £100. Jimmy with Alice (blonde). Charlie dies; Jimmy promises to marry Moira. Marriage (church, rain). Moira's child born (girl, dark eyes).

**Ch III "Two Ways of Love"**: Jimmy and Moira estranged; letters; Jimmy engaged to Alice; ASHBY FEAK (explorer) rival; Moira finds Jimmy; Alice engaged to Ashby Feak.

**Ch IV "The Long Night"**: Ditchburn finds Moira's letters (addressed "James Larrance, Esq."), gives them to Jimmy; Jimmy drinks, nearly kills? (threatens Moira); Jimmy writes at Moira's urging; Moira's letters (unsent): "I LOVE YOU"; "The child is yours."

**Ch V "If I Might Die!"**: Ditchburn reveals to Moira; she flees with child; Patience; Jimmy hunts her.

**Ch VI "The Spirit of Old Paul"**: Jimmy takes child to Daisley Cross; Moira returns; Jimmy confesses love; "She's mine"; they reunite at Old Paul's grave. THE END.

---

## BOOK 2 — The Crow's Inn Tragedy (Annie Haynes)

**Ch I**: Crow's Inn, Messrs. Bechcombe & Turner, offices, 1st floor, No. 21. LUKE BECHCOMBE (solicitor, small, spare, grey beard, horn-rimmed spectacles, widower? wife MADELINE). Rev. JAMES COLLYER (rector of Wexbridge, Luke's brother-in-law; sister Mrs. Collyer). Son ANTHONY "TONY" COLLYER (WWI veteran, D.S.O., idle, debts). Tony to be bear-leader; engaged to CECILY HOYLE (Luke's secretary). AUBREY TODMARSH (Tony's cousin, conscientious objector, Community of St. Philip; engaged to Mrs. Phillimore, rich American widow). Emerald cross (Collyer heirloom) brought by Collyer to Luke for sale; Luke finds stones paste. Mention "Yellow Gang"/Yellow Dog.

**Ch II**: South London Settlement, Confraternity of St. Philip (Aubrey). Michael Farmore arrested; HOPKINS (Aubrey's man, dark eyes, mouth opening/shutting). Tony visits; Mrs. Phillimore in car.

**Ch III**: Office day, Tony goes round to private door; AMOS THOMPSON (managing clerk, horn-rimmed glasses, missing teeth, brown beard); Bank messenger; clerks SPENCER & JOHN WALLS find Luke dead (strangled, chloroform), key missing; Dr. HACKETT. Cecily Hoyle found.

**Ch IV**: Inspector FURNIVAL ("The Ferret", Scotland Yard). Cecily says she met Tony; white glove found; Spencer saw lady with yellow hair; Tony's alibi. Rector reports.

**Ch V**: Tony & Aubrey quarrel; Mrs. Bechcombe; John STEADMAN (K.C., cousin, criminologist). Thompson's room in Brooklyn Terrace, North Kensington (No. 10); photo of Cecily; library book (detective novel).

**Ch VI**: Brooklyn Terrace search; library clerk describes Thompson.

**Ch VII**: Auditors: defalcations. Rubber gloves. Aubrey reports Hopkins saw Thompson at docks. Lady with glove telephones Yard.

**Ch VIII**: Mrs. CARNTHWACKE (Cyril B. Carnthwacke's wife, ex-actress Bella Laymond) visits; sold diamonds to Luke (receipt); diamonds missing from safe.

**Ch IX**: Cecily interview; Cecily's permanent address (Miss Cochrane, Morley House, Beesford); Steadman offers job; Walls/Spencer; telegram "Do not mention home address. Father." Burford (New Forest) rumoured.

**Ch X**: Burford; Rose Cottage; Christopher Hoyle, painter; fake signatures.

**Ch XI**: Cecily meets Tony at Kensington Gardens; says she's leaving him; reveals secret; Steadman offers Tony post at Bramley Hall (Sir John Bramley).

**Ch XII**: Carnthwacke at Yard: Fédora (fortune-teller) leaked diamonds plan.

**Ch XIII**: Tony sees Cecily with man (Hoyle); Hopkins arrested at Whistone Hall (Sir Thomas Wreford); Aubrey distressed; Ditchburn? no.

**Ch XIV**: Luncheon; Mrs. Carnthwacke says portrait not Luke; "man impersonated Luke"; Carnthwacke: murderer.

**Ch XV**: Mrs. Carnthwacke describes man: thumbs/forefingers unusual, hair low on forehead; Mrs. Phillimore doubts.

**Ch XVI**: Rector finds emerald news; reads note burnt; blood on blotter.

**Ch XVII**: Emeralds recovered; Brunton (clerk) overheard Thompson & Cecily in fog; Lim-house meeting 21 Burlase Street, "Chink-a-pin".

**Ch XVIII**: Cecily's letter; Cecily's secret; Thompson-Hoyle; Hoyle's train; tramp; Masterman identifies "Samuel Horsingforth, Sta. Irica, Portugal."

**Ch XIX**: Mrs. Carnthwacke attacked (cord); Steadman to Carnthwacke's; female guards.

**Ch XX**: Thompson arrested at Southampton (as Samuel Horsingforth, alias John Frederick Hoyle).

**Ch XXI**: Disguise by marmoset-faced man in Soho; Golden Room; Yellow Dog in dais; trapped.

**Ch XXII**: Steadman & Furnival stripped, bound, thrown in room; escape by knife note ("from one who is grateful").

**Ch XXIII**: Swim; police launch; house raid; Yellow Room; Gordon removes staircase; fire.

**Ch XXIV**: Community tea; Hopkins welcome; Todmarsh arrested as Yellow Dog (thumb/forefinger, cyanide fake). Hopkins' wife rescued child. Tony & Cecily reconcile; "The End."
